summary: Curiosity is humanity's utmost feature that we must express. Through science, we best feel the thrill of knowledge and community. Team Challenger Seekers addresses this specific challenge to show that what we know and have is not the limit to what there is. Reading through the available Earth analogs for Mars and the Moon sparked a need to discover new characteristics that can help and provide use to NASA and other space agencies. In this project, we made it our ultimate goal to help our minds by learning in this experience and, more importantly, contribute to society's achievements and progression. Engaging with one another in actions and will has gotten us so far throughout histroy and can only continue to do so. We researched possible analog locations on Earth and analyized data from NASA and other credible sources to ensure a valid and smooth project. We covered deserts, polar regions, volcanic & arid terrains as well as caves. We followed exact scientific method sequences that not only remove worry for scientists but also provide new insights and discoveries that can be effective in their missions. All of our observations have been presented with the best methods one could understand: visuals, interactive maps, and graphs to further confirm the math and thought processes are as accurate as possible. As two seniors in high school with an intermediate level of experience in this field, we are grateful and ready to take on this challenge and be judged.
details:
Hello! This is Team Challenger Seekers speaking. We want to note that there was use of AI during this project. What we personally did was research databases and compile all the information and resources to use; we then worked together, read through the websites, and gathered details. During this process, we used the help of ChatGPT to further validate our findings & also used Claude for help with interactive features and overall checking. We hope our work benefits scientists & engineers, and we hope you enjoy the reading journey, as we enjoyed the experience of this challenge!!

We considered some data limitations and the fact that not all conditions must be satisfied for an analog to be valid; as long as one is true and is genuinely useful for astronauts, then it would still be suitable in the study. Alongside that, we incorporated every minor and major detail worthy of note, such as impact on human biology, EVA engineering components, operational cost, and lithology. We used the above to determine a credible grading system for the characteristics of each new analog with rescept mars and the Moon. We considered the new math that we'd be learning and included statistical measures and formulas to further show accuracy in graphs and in formats like log, etc that would help the scale at which information is presented.
